allowedSourceMaterial.overview: A young man carrying a big basket that contains his extremely deformed, formerly conjoined twin brother seeks vengeance on the doctors who separated them against their will.

facts.overview: A young man carrying a big basket that contains his extremely deformed, formerly conjoined twin brother seeks vengeance on the doctors who separated them against their will.
facts.title: Basket Case

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: What happens when the hidden brother inside the basket is finally unleashed against the surgeons who cut them apart?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Carrying a large wicker basket that hides his severely deformed, formerly conjoined twin brother, a young man arrives in the city seeking bloody vengeance against the doctors who separated them against their will.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Grimy, suspenseful horror-comedy with heavy undertones, balancing shocking absurdity with a steady, focused pace.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Frank Henenlotter blends grotesque horror with pitch-black comedy, delivering a singular revenge tale driven by macabre brotherly devotion and pure midnight-movie energy.

issueSummaries: description: 'a young man arrives in the city' specifies a location (the city) not established anywhere in the authorized overview, which contains no setting/location detail beyond the characters and premise.
description: 'wicker basket' concretizes the basket's material, a specific factual attribute not supported by the overview's generic 'big basket.'

curiosityHook: 'the hidden brother inside the basket is finally unleashed against the surgeons' shifts agency to the twin brother acting against the surgeons, whereas the overview attributes the vengeance-seeking specifically to 'a young man,' with the brother as a carried, deformed figure rather than an established independent agent of the revenge.
claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: Per A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1, low-risk atmospheric and genre shorthand is tolerated, but 'arrives in the city' and 'wicker basket' add unsupported concrete factual attributes (location, material) not established by the closed-world source. More significantly, curiosityHook's framing of the brother being 'unleashed' against the surgeons reassigns agency for the vengeance from the young man (as stated in the overview) to the twin, which is a minor but meaningful shift in decision-relevant character/motive framing. These are bounded, fixable overstatements rather than severe distortions of plot mechanics or spoiler-boundary violations, so MINOR is appropriate.

sourceEvidence.notes: Overview supports: a young man carries a big basket containing his extremely deformed, formerly conjoined twin brother, and seeks vengeance on the doctors who separated them against their will.
